reason: It holds up on feasibility and schedule. It changes the lab only: no kernel, no submission change (so the submission stays byte-identical trivially), 0 s of hidden-run time, no LB slot. The lab defect is real. The DIVINS_CALL in tools/build_probe_kernel.py (l.321-337) calls score_nodes without model_index, so p is the mean of the 5 v1 fold models (tools/daughternet.py l.115-129). trainlab node_p_from_divins/insert35 (l.350-383) use that p, and v1 was trained on all 199 clips (CONTEXT l.1275). Timing works: shard A was pushed 17:15 UTC, shard B follows FF (~20:00 UTC), and the OOF run (~0.3-0.5 GPU-h vs ~5 h quota left before the reset, estimate) can land ~21:30-22:00 UTC, before T9 (26 Sep 06:30-09:00). It is not on the K2/K3 critical path. Caveats that shrink it to a guard only. (1) The insertion check is already non-binding: T9 and trainlab.gates l.662-668 say 'R2 unchanged, LB decides'. OOF arms therefore cannot change K2/K3; they only make the CONTEXT warning honest. (2) Reading (b) conflicts with the binding rules. It adopts nosteal0 as a K-rider on lab evidence of >= +2 net TP. R2 allows 'only the #35 config, no ladders', and R4 says fork-set changers need LB delta >= +0.002, never lab gain alone. A ~1-event change cannot reach +0.002, so nosteal0 is effectively closed whatever the lab says. (3) Silent wrong-model risk. kds_core.discover_checkpoints finds only fold_k/best.pt, taking the fold from the directory name (l.203-248). The kernel's v1 weights are flat vitalii_daughternet/fold_0..4.pt. The kdn-score kernel-metadata attaches the LATEST biohub-l2-kdn-train output, likely DaughterNet v2 (kdn-train v3, CONTEXT l.1314). The ens==dump contract would catch that, but only after a wasted run.
